title: [Plan] DIR-054: Eliminate 429 Storm on /api/messages/conversations, Shared Poller Architecture & Rate-Limit Alignment
body: DIR-054 FORENSIC RCA VALIDATED AGAINST SOURCE (measured, not assumed). RCA-1 CONFIRMED AND AMPLIFIED: FOUR independent hook instances mount, not three - CubaCandidateShell.jsx:170, MessagesNavBadge.jsx:74, ProfileDisplay.jsx:34, EmployerSidebar.jsx:194. At POLL_INTERVAL_MS=15000 that is 16 req/min = 80 requests per 5-minute window against a 30-request budget, so the quota is exhausted in about 1.9 minutes and every later tick 429s - exactly the 52-error console storm the User reported. RCA-2 CONFIRMED: backend/security/abuse.js:132-136 declares MESSAGING_FIVE_MINUTE_LIMIT default 30 over windowMs 300000, and backend/index.js:554 mounts it globally on all of /api/messages, so GET badge reads share one budget with POST mutations. generalApiLimiter (120/min, index.js:482-485) is NOT the binding constraint. RCA-3 CONFIRMED: useUnreadMessages.js:99 uses a fixed setInterval(refresh, POLL_INTERVAL_MS) and the catch at :64-68 only sets status error, so the timer keeps firing forever with zero Retry-After respect and zero backoff. RCA-4 CONFIRMED: apiJson (platform.js:170-191) issues a bare fetch with cache no-store, no in-flight promise reuse and no TTL - unlike the proven fetchPublicConfig precedent (platform.js:150-168: publicConfigInFlight + PUBLIC_CONFIG_TTL_MS=15000 snapshot) which should be mirrored. RCA-5 CONFIRMED WITH EXACT EVIDENCE: node --test tests/dir023-contrast-tokens.test.mjs yields 14 pass / 1 FAIL - unmapped light-shade opacity classes: bg-amber-50/95, border-amber-300/70, dark:text-amber-100/80 - all three originating from the DIR-053 reconnect banner at src/components/Candidate/CubaCandidateHero.jsx:201 and :206. CORRECTION TO THE SPEC: the directive names src/components/cuba/CubaCandidateHero.jsx, which DOES NOT EXIST; the real file is src/components/Candidate/CubaCandidateHero.jsx. CONSTRAINTS THAT MUST SURVIVE: tests/messaging-module-gate.test.mjs:112 pins /POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 15000/, :113 pins addEventListener focus refresh, :101 pins the exact returned object shape, :105 pins data totalUnread, :108/:109 pin the fail-visible error path, :116-120 pin resolveMessagesVisibility and setModuleEnabled(false), :123 forbids conf/fire. cuba-tokens.css (2591 lines) currently contains ZERO dark:-prefixed doubled selectors, so inventing one is riskier than reusing already-mapped classes. PLAN: S1 split the coarse messaging limiter into a generous READ tier (namespace messaging-read, MESSAGING_READ_FIVE_MINUTE_LIMIT default 300 per 5 min = 60/min, 3.75x headroom over the post-S2 worst case of 16/min, failClosed false per the publicBrowse/generalApi coarse-tier precedent) applied only to GET/HEAD on /api/messages/conversations, plus the mutation tier raised from 30 to 150 per spec S1 while KEEPING failClosed true because a mutation budget must stay fail-closed; register both env keys in backend/services/platformConfiguration.js around line 150; preserve the DIR-026 module gate ordering at index.js:571 and the post-requireAuth mount. S2 convert useUnreadMessages.js into a module-level singleton store (subscribers Set + shared snapshot + inflight promise + lastFetchedAt) so exactly ONE interval and ONE network read exist no matter how many components mount, keeping the literal POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 15000, the window focus listener, and the exact returned contract; every consumer reads the same snapshot so all four call sites stay identical and truthful. S3 replace the fixed interval with a self-scheduling setTimeout loop and a Retry-After circuit breaker - extend apiJson ADDITIVELY to attach err.retryAfter from the response Retry-After header (response headers are currently discarded at platform.js:182-189) - with exponential backoff 15s to 30s to 60s to 120s to 240s capped at 300s, resetting to 15s on any success, and logging the outage transition ONCE instead of per tick. S4 fix the contrast regression at the component, which is the option the spec authorises, by using already-mapped classes: bg-amber-50/95 to bg-amber-50/90 (mapped at cuba-tokens.css:1941), border-amber-300/70 to border-amber-300/80 (mapped at cuba-tokens.css:2203), and dark:text-amber-100/80 to the bare dark:text-amber-100. Deliberately NOT adding new !important maps, because a doubled-selector !important rule for bg-amber-50/95 or border-amber-300/70 would beat the banner own dark:bg-amber-500/10 and dark:border-amber-400/40 overrides and re-create the very pastel-island defect DIR-023 exists to prevent. Net result: 15/15 green with ZERO CSS churn. S5 verification: npm run test:security:static, npm run lint, npm test, npm run build under the 4.0s budget, a new regression suite pinning single-interval coalescing, the backoff ladder, Retry-After honouring and the 300/150 defaults, and a live XAMPP-served Playwright capture of https://ime365.local/dashboard for at least 6 continuous minutes asserting 0 x 429 on /api/messages/conversations, exactly one request per 15s tick, 0 console errors and clean badge sync, then bridge dev submit-evidence. All servers strictly via XAMPP; no detached background server processes.

steps: S1 backend/security/abuse.js - add messagingReadAccountLimiter (namespace messaging-read, MESSAGING_READ_FIVE_MINUTE_LIMIT default 300 per 5min, failClosed false) and raise messagingAccountLimiter default 30 to 150 (failClosed true stays)
export both
S2 backend/services/platformConfiguration.js - register MESSAGING_READ_FIVE_MINUTE_LIMIT alongside MESSAGING_FIVE_MINUTE_LIMIT so the admin panel can tune both

S3 backend/index.js line 554 - replace the blanket app.use /api/messages messagingAccountLimiter mount with a method-aware dispatcher routing GET/HEAD to messagingReadAccountLimiter and all other methods to messagingAccountLimiter, keeping the DIR-026 module gate at line 571 after it and after requireAuth
S4 src/services/api/platform.js apiJson - additively attach err.retryAfter from the Retry-After response header, no change to existing callers

S5 src/hooks/useUnreadMessages.js - extract a module-level singleton store (subscribers Set, shared snapshot, inflight promise, lastFetchedAt) with exactly one refcounted scheduler shared by all consumers, preserving POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 15000, the window focus listener and the returned { unreadCount, error, status, enabled, refresh } object

S6 src/hooks/useUnreadMessages.js - replace setInterval with a self-scheduling setTimeout loop implementing exponential backoff 15s/30s/60s/120s/240s capped at 300s, honouring Retry-After on 429 and 503, resetting to 15s on success and logging the outage transition once
S7 src/components/Candidate/CubaCandidateHero.jsx lines 201 and 206 - swap bg-amber-50/95 to bg-amber-50/90, border-amber-300/70 to border-amber-300/80, dark:text-amber-100/80 to dark:text-amber-100
S8 add regression tests covering poller coalescing, the backoff ladder, Retry-After honouring and the read/mutation limiter split
S9 run npm run test:security:static, npm run lint, npm test, npm run build
S10 live XAMPP Playwright 6-minute dashboard poll capture asserting 0 x 429 and 0 console errors, saved under .bridge/evidence/

title: [P0] DIR-055: Unified Executive Builder Header ("Best of Both Worlds") & Real Interactive Notifications Pipeline
body:
### 1. MANDATE & PROBLEM STATEMENT
The User compared the legacy Resume Builder header with the current interface and inspected the Notifications popover on https://ime365.local/dashboard.
The User strictly commands:
'this is my old header but new one is not as good as this. can you get the best of both worlds? Add New directive. Also Notifications are not real, not working. ask developer to fix this pipeline After the current one is done'.
Mandate:
1. Merge the rich functional ergonomics of the legacy Resume Builder header (prominent Dashboard exit, editable title, template selector dropdown pill, live save beacon, ATS score pill with drawer trigger, Share, Sync Profile, Preview, and Download CTAs, plus the horizontal step ribbon with completed checkmarks and progress overview) with the modern Cuba glassmorphic design system ('best of both worlds'), eliminating any double-header clutter.
2. Completely overhaul the Notifications pipeline: eliminate stale duplicate placeholders ('New message 4d ago'), resolve real navigable hrefs per notification type, add working 'Mark all as read' and per-row read toggles, and wire real MariaDB notification generation with sender/snippet grounding.

### 2. ROOT CAUSE & ARCHITECTURAL SPECIFICATION
1. RCA-1 (Builder Header Layout & Feature Regression):
   In BuildResume.jsx and AuthenticatedAppShell.jsx, mounting inside CubaCandidateShell can lead to dual topbar crowding or suppression of dedicated builder controls. The legacy header provided superior density:
   - Left: '<- Dashboard' pill, title rename, template selector dropdown pill ('Professional Classic v'), and live 'Saved' beacon.
   - Center: Interactive ATS pill ('ATS: 39/100 | Getting Started v') opening the ATS score breakdown drawer.
   - Right: 'Share', 'Sync Profile', 'Preview' (eye icon), and high-contrast 'Download' CTA.
   - Ribbon: Horizontal stepper with '<' / '>' scroll arrows, completed green checkmarks '(v)', active step pill, and 'X of 10 complete - XX% v' overview trigger.
2. RCA-2 (Dead & Fake Notifications Pipeline):
   - In MariaDB 'notifications', 25 stale identical rows ('New message / You have a new message' 4d ago) exist without sender attribution.
   - In M3NotificationCenter.jsx, 'onClick={() => onNavigate?.(item.href)}' is completely dead because 'notifications' rows do NOT store or return an 'href'. Clicks fail silently.
   - No 'Mark all as read' action exists in the UI; unread badge remains permanently stuck at 25.
   - 'onOpenAll' redirects blindly to '/dashboard' instead of a real notifications/activity destination.

### 3. TECHNICAL IMPLEMENTATION STEPS (S1 - S6)
- S1: Unified 'Best of Both Worlds' Builder Header in BuildResume.jsx
  - Redesign BuildResume header into a premium Cuba glassmorphic surface (backdrop-blur, refined slate/cuba border tokens, full dark-mode compatibility).
  - Cleanly integrate or adapt the shell so the builder presents a dedicated, un-crowded topbar with:
    * '<- Dashboard' exit pill.
    * Click-to-edit resume title + template selector dropdown pill (Cv1-Cv51 with search/preview).
    * Live auto-save beacon ('* Saved' / 'Saving...' / 'Error').
    * Interactive ATS score pill with tone color and drawer trigger.
    * Quick Actions: 'Share', 'Sync Profile', 'Preview' (eye icon), and high-contrast primary 'Download'.
  - Elevate the Horizontal Step Navigation Ribbon: '<' and '>' scroll arrows, completed green checkmark pills, active step highlighting, and 'X of 10 complete - XX%' overview trigger.
- S2: Real Navigable Hrefs & Bulk Read in Backend
  - In backend/routes/notificationsData.js and backend/repositories/MySQLRepository.js:
    * Map each notification row to a real client 'href':
      - message -> '/dashboard/messages?conversation=' + (data.conversationId || '')
      - application -> '/dashboard/jobs'
      - interview -> '/dashboard/interviews'
      - system -> '/dashboard'
    * Add 'POST /api/notifications-data/mark-all-read' marking all rows for req.user.uid as is_read = 1.
- S3: Interactive Notifications UI in M3NotificationCenter.jsx
  - Add 'Mark all as read' button in popover header calling 'POST /api/notifications-data/mark-all-read'.
  - Make notification rows interactive: clicking marks the individual notification as read ('PATCH /api/notifications-data/:id') and routes to 'item.href'.
  - Render contextual icons (message icon for messages, briefcases for job applications, calendars for interviews).
  - Format honest relative timestamps and clean empty state ('You are all caught up') when all are read.
- S4: Real Notification Generation in Backend
  - In backend/index.js message sending route ('POST /api/messages/conversations/:id/messages'), ensure notifications include real sender name, conversation ID, and message snippet in data.
  - Mark or clean up the stale 4-day-old duplicate test notifications in MariaDB for uid OhZdiSIFL7ePA1TMkfu9bnR935D3.
- S5: Responsive Validation & Accessibility
  - Verify builder header and step ribbon across 375px, 768px, and 1280px viewports with zero horizontal overflow or clipping.
  - Ensure all buttons have unique aria-labels and keyboard focus rings.
- S6: E2E Verification & Evidence Pack
  - Author regression tests for notification routes (href resolution, mark-all-read).
  - Run npm test, npm run lint, and Playwright DOM crawl verifying:
    1. Builder header renders 'best of both worlds' controls cleanly.
    2. Notifications open, navigate to real links, mark as read, and update badge in real time.

### 4. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- AC-1: Resume Builder presents the complete 'best of both worlds' header (Dashboard exit, title, template selector, live save status, ATS pill, Share, Sync Profile, Preview, Download, and completed checkmark stepper ribbon) in premium Cuba styling.
- AC-2: Notifications popover displays real, non-placeholder notifications with actionable navigation hrefs.
- AC-3: Clicking a notification navigates to its destination and marks it as read.
- AC-4: 'Mark all as read' clears the unread badge and updates MariaDB state.
- AC-5: 0 console errors, 100% test pass in npm test, and zero regression against frozen baselines.

That distinction changes the fix from rewriting the producer to remediating legacy rows plus wiring navigation. (6) The token layer the Lead asks me to define is already complete and certified by DIR-048: cuba-tokens.css has --cuba-glass-bg and --cuba-glass-border and --cuba-glass-blur at 185-189, --cuba-shadow-xl at 243, scrollbar tokens at 247-249, --cuba-z-popover 70 at 261, --cuba-header-menu-border at 270, --cuba-popover-bg at 278, --cuba-header-divider at 279, --cuba-header-badge-fill at 285, dark overrides at 469-493 and 556-570, and the Tailwind bridge at 634-656, while cuba-glass, cuba-popover, cuba-scrollbar and cuba-focusable already exist as classes. I will REUSE these and invent zero new tokens, because inventing parallel tokens is the actual regression risk. (7) Every UX state the Lead demands already has a primitive: CubaSkeleton, CubaEmptyState, CubaErrorState, CubaDrawer, CubaInlineNotice, CubaModal all exist under src/components/cuba. CONTRACT BOUNDARIES AND INVARIANTS: ZERO database schema change, the notifications table at 001_baseline.sql:369-386 is untouched and its data JSON column is the only extension point, so no migration is added and the MariaDB schema baseline stays at diff 0. The only new route is POST /api/notifications-data/mark-all-read, owner-scoped with WHERE user_id = ? AND is_read = 0, and it cannot collide with the pinned forbidden regex router.post single-quote slash colon id at tests/notification-lifecycle.test.mjs:25. The href is the Lead-approved /dashboard/messages. ### 2. CORE RESPONSIBILITY (DEVELOPER-AUTHORED SUB-DIRECTIVES)
The Developer must NOT wait for the user or Lead to hand over individual bug reports. The Developer must:
1. Conduct deep forensic discovery across the real codebase, database, routes, and UI.
2. Formulate and construct specific, actionable engineering sub-directives for every discovered defect.
3. Submit the sub-directives to the Lead Supervisor for formal review.
4. STRICT APPROVAL GATE: The Developer must NOT begin unapproved implementation until the Lead Supervisor verifies the findings, evaluates trade-offs, and issues the explicit GREEN SIGNAL approval for each sub-directive.

### 3. MANDATORY DISCOVERY SURFACES
A. Architecture & Backend Boundaries: API contracts, authentication/authorization, tenant isolation, database integrity, error responses.
B. Dashboard Completeness: Candidate, Employer, and Admin dashboards; verify real MariaDB data hydration vs hardcoded/empty stubs, accurate KPIs, and responsive layouts.
C. UI/UX, Interaction & Modals: Every route, button, modal, popup, and navigation link must have a verified outcome (zero dead views, blank screens, or unstyled dialogs).
D. System-Wide Document Print, PDF & Export Pipelines: Audit all print and export surfaces across the codebase (including recruiter applicant resume printing in EmployerApplicantPipeline, cover letters, invoices, interview coaching, and all 51 CV templates) to eliminate unstyled iframes, unconstrained avatars/photos, and multi-page whitespace sprawl.
E. Business Logic & Integrations: End-to-end data flow (e.g. Job Applications vs Kanban Job Tracker, saved favorites across documents and jobs, billing coupons vs module toggles).

### 4. MANDATORY 10-POINT FORMAT FOR EACH SUB-DIRECTIVE
Every sub-directive proposed by the Developer must provide:
1. Directive Title & Proposed ID
2. Evidence & Findings (exact file paths, line numbers, routes, reproduction steps, current vs expected)
3. Objective
4. Scope (files/modules changed, boundaries, exclusions)
5. Implementation Strategy
6. Acceptance Criteria (measurable, observable conditions)
7. Verification Plan (unit, integration, Playwright E2E, DOM crawl)
8. Risks & Dependencies
9. Priority & Severity (P0, P1, P2, P3)
10. Estimated Effort

### 5. EXECUTION SEQUENCE
- Step 1: Execute systematic forensic discovery across the codebase.
- Step 2: Author the Master Enhancement Backlog and detailed sub-directives.
- Step 3: Submit the proposed sub-directives via bridge dev plan for Lead review.
- Step 4: Await Lead approval before writing implementation code.

title: [P0] DIR-064: DIR-064: Eliminate PDF Blank Page & Skip-Link Bleed, Fix Footer Overlap (Certification Card Geometry), and Centralized Cross-Platform Export Pipeline
body:
### 1. EXECUTIVE MISSION & PROBLEM STATEMENT
Live user inspection identified three critical defects in resume export and visual pagination:
1. PDF Export First Page Blank with Skip-link Banner: In generated PDFs, Page 1 is almost entirely blank except for an accessibility button Skip to main content rendered at the top, pushing the entire resume to Page 2. Root Cause: .skip-link in index.html has no @media print suppression rules.
2. Content Overlapping and Bleeding Under Page Footer: Multi-item cards (such as Certifications with 2-line titles, issuer lines, and badges e.g. CCRN) bleed directly into and behind .smart-page-footer (Babu M ... 1/1). Root Cause: smartPartitioner.js estimates certification row height at only 52px whereas actual cards take 74px-85px, and .smart-page-body lacks a protective safety buffer above the footer.
3. Cross-Platform Centralized Single-Source Downloader Pipeline: Production deployment is on a standard Linux server. The codebase must NEVER depend on Windows-native tools (winget, PowerShell scripts, Windows-only paths). Downloader logic must be unified into a single cross-platform client (src/utils/exportDownloader.js) for both PDF and DOCX.

### 2. DELIVERABLES
1. Eliminate skip-link and leading blank page in PDF export (add @media print display:none, remove in Exporter.jsx and backend/index.js before page.pdf()).
2. Recalibrate certification row height estimator in smartPartitioner.js (~76px-84px per row + title margin) and add safe bottom clearance in smartEngine.css so cards never collide with the footer.
3. Create centralized single-source downloader src/utils/exportDownloader.js with magic-byte validation (%PDF- and PK zip) and refactor all consumer portals to use it.
4. Verify 100% Linux server compatibility with pure Node.js and Playwright Chromium headless flags.

### 3. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA & EVIDENCE
- Exported PDF starts on Page 1 with resume content and zero blank pages or skip-link text.
- Certification cards have zero overlap or clipping with page footer.
- Centralized export downloader module created and integrated across all portal surfaces.
- 100% test pass on PDF and DOCX export suites with clean build.

CONFIRMED FACTS: docxExport.js assembles ONE Section whose children are a single 2-column table, which is exactly why the 34% sidebar band persists on Page 2+; docx is v9.5.1 and exposes ImageRun, SectionType and ShadingType; the builder has NO image support today; and the employer-resume route GET /api/employer/jobs/:jobId/applications/:applicationId/resume already authorizes a recruiter by job.employerId === req.user.uid plus an application whose jobId matches and whose resumeId identifies the candidate resume, and it returns a DRAFT resume too. IMPORTANT CONFLICT I WILL NOT PAPER OVER: the mandate says the draft-status DOCX gate should 'match recruiter PDF export permissions', but the recruiter PDF path uses /api/public-export, which is PUBLISHED-ONLY. Simply deleting the published-only check on /api/public-export-docx would be a real IDOR hole (any authenticated stranger could export any draft by guessing a resumeId). I will therefore implement the gate as an explicit, verifiable employer claim instead: when the caller is authenticated AND supplies jobId plus applicationId, the server re-verifies ownership and the application-to-resume binding and then permits a draft export; every other request keeps the strict published-only rule. (1) MULTI-PAGE FULL-WIDTH REFLOW: split the 2-column builders into Section 1 (the sidebar|hero table carrying page-1 content) followed by a next-page section break, and Section 2 emitting the continuation content as FULL-WIDTH paragraphs/tables, matching the PDF smart-main-content--full and removing the blank sidebar band; a single section is kept when everything fits page 1. I will be explicit that the split is a conservative budget heuristic, not a true paginator. (2) ARCHETYPE CERT PARITY: flip the two buildCertificationsBlock calls in buildExecutiveBannerDocument and buildTechGridDocument from columns 1 to columns 2. (3) PHOTO EMBEDDING: resolve resume.photo from a validated base64 data URL (png/jpeg mime plus a byte cap) or a remote https URL fetched through a strict host allowlist with a byte cap and timeout, embed it with ImageRun in the identity/sidebar header at a bounded size, and omit it gracefully on any failure so a bad photo can never break an export. (4) SKILLS PILLS: render non-inline skills as shaded F1F5F9 pill runs with padding instead of raw bullets, keeping the inline and rating variants and a linear reading order. (5) FREE-TIER WATERMARK: when resume._watermark.enableFreeWatermark is true, add the branded 'Created with IME365 (Free Plan)' footer tag, and wire that flag into both DOCX routes exactly as the PDF route computes it. UX STATES: a missing photo, an absent watermark and an empty section must all degrade silently rather than emit a placeholder heading; a failed export must still fail loudly with the existing error contract. ACCESSIBILITY: shaded pills keep their text contrast at or above 4.5:1 against F1F5F9, the photo carries no meaning that is lost when omitted, and the DOCX reading order stays linear for screen readers. body: DIR-069 COMPLETE - true DOCX/PDF parity across six mandates plus the recruiter draft gate. (1) MULTI-PAGE FULL-WIDTH REFLOW: docxExport.js previously emitted ONE Section whose children were a single 2-column table, so Word reserved the 34% sidebar band on EVERY page. Added splitHeroForPageOne (a conservative node-height budget of 12200 twips) and twoColumnWithReflow; the Modern Split, Executive Banner and Tech Grid builders now return { children, continuation }, and resumeDocument emits the continuation as a SECOND Section with SectionType.NEXT_PAGE so page 2+ is 100 percent full width, matching the PDF smart-main-content--full. A one-page resume stays a single section. (2) ARCHETYPE CERT PARITY: the two buildCertificationsBlock calls in buildExecutiveBannerDocument and buildTechGridDocument flipped from columns 1 to columns 2, so every archetype matches the PDF 2-column card grid. (3) PHOTO EMBEDDING: imported ImageRun and added decodeDataUrlPhoto (validated image/png or image/jpeg base64 with a 2MB cap), fetchRemotePhoto (https-only against a 3-host image-CDN allowlist, redirect disabled, 5s timeout, 2MB cap, image/* content-type required) and buildPhotoParagraph; buildIdentityHeader leads with the headshot (so the sidebar header variant inherits it), and resolveResumePhoto runs in createResumeDocx before the synchronous build. Any failure, including a non-allowlisted or loopback host, is non-fatal and the photo is simply omitted. (4) SKILL PILLS: non-inline skills are no longer raw bullets; they render as shaded F1F5F9 pill runs with padding, keeping the inline and rating variants and a linear reading order. (5) FREE-TIER WATERMARK: when resume._watermark.enableFreeWatermark is true the section footer carries the branded 'Created with IME365 (Free Plan)' tag; both DOCX routes now compute the same isPaidOwner flag the PDF route uses, so free-tier DOCX matches the PDF (a branded footer tag, which the mandate explicitly permits as an alternative to a diagonal watermark). (6) RECRUITER DRAFT GATE: POST /api/public-export-docx now has an explicit, server-verified employer-claim branch - when the caller is authenticated and supplies jobId plus applicationId, the server re-verifies job.employerId === req.user.uid AND that the application belongs to that job AND that its resumeId equals the requested resumeId AND then loads the draft resume; every other request keeps the strict published-only rule. I did NOT simply delete the published-only check (that would have been a real IDOR hole). The drawer now forwards the claim (jobId/applicationId) through exportDownloader, so the path is wired end to end. (7) GUARDS: src/cv-templates git diff = 0, 100 percent Linux compatible, zero OS console windows. EVIDENCE: new tests/dir069-docx-parity.test.mjs 13/13 - static contracts for all seven mandates plus FUNCTIONAL proofs: a data-URL photo lands in word/media with a w:drawing and its absence produces no media part; a loopback photo URL is refused and the export still succeeds; the watermark reaches word/footer1.xml while a paid export has none; skills emit w:fill=F1F5F9; a 24-role resume emits a nextPage section while a one-page resume does not; executive-banner and tech-grid emit equal-width 2-column certification card tables; and the drawer forwards the employer claim. Regression: dir063..069 + previews + empty-sections + dir048/055/056 + employer + fouc 153/153; backend DOCX/parity/export-pipeline 38/38; full control surface 2090/2090; product + design-system + dashboard + employer slice 147/147. SUPERSEDED CONTRACTS UPDATED: dir067 S4 and dir068 previously asserted that the public DOCX route never reads req.user.uid; DIR-069 legitimately requires that read inside the verified employer claim, so both now assert the stronger contract - the only owner read is the job-ownership check, and the published-only rule remains the fallback. HONEST LIMITS: (a) the page-1/continuation split is a conservative node-height HEURISTIC, not a paginator, so a pathological page-1 overflow could still carry the table onto page 2; (b) the free-tier DOCX mark is a branded FOOTER TAG, not a true Word diagonal watermark; (c) photo support is base64 data URLs plus a 3-host image-CDN allowlist - other hosts (including the app's own storage origin) are refused and the photo is omitted; (d) the recruiter draft gate is IDOR-safe by construction and unit-verified, but I did NOT exercise a live authenticated draft export against a live MariaDB; (e) scripts/verify-zero-broken-routes.mjs and tests/full-system-audit.mjs need a live host and were not run.

body: DIR-070 P0, reconnaissance complete on the 665-line partitioner I already know well from DIR-065/067. CONTRACTS/INVARIANTS: src/cv-templates stays git diff 0, the DIR-063..069 suites and the census/overflow gates stay green, no detached server or Windows-only tooling, and the estimator must always equal what the renderer paints (otherwise the footer-overlap bug returns). ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED: applyOrphanGuard (added in DIR-067 mandate 2B) moves a whole stranded section onto the last page when that page holds a single row of a section continuing from an earlier page. For the Babu M profile only the trailing CCRN card spills, so the guard drags the other four certifications off Page 1 and leaves a 250-300px blank void under Projects. SECOND CONFIRMED LIMIT: micro-compaction only varies sectionGapPx (14 to 11), which reclaims about 12px, while Babu M overflows by roughly 27px, so it can never fit. (1) MULTI-TIER ADAPTIVE MICRO-COMPACTION: introduce a COMPACTION_TIERS table - tier 0 is the density default, tier 1 tightens the section rhythm (14 to 11px), tier 2 tightens the section rhythm to 9-10px AND the grid row gap (7 to 5px) AND the card padding (7 to 5px) AND the title/item margins, reclaiming up to ~70px in total. Because the grid estimators are built before packing, I will extract the section building into a buildSections(tier) closure so each tier recomputes card geometry from its own padding and row gap, then adopt the FIRST tier that fits one page. (2) PAGE 1 VOID PREVENTION INVARIANT: applyOrphanGuard will compute the donor page's void after a proposed move and REFUSE the move whenever the void would exceed 80px or 10 percent of the usable capacity, so the guard can never again leave Page 1 half-empty. (3) BALANCED 2-PAGE DISTRIBUTION: keep greedy page-1 filling (split a section whenever at least one row fits) and, when a section genuinely cannot start, choose the smallest possible void; assert Page 1 fills to at least 85 percent of capacity whenever two pages are produced. (4) RENDER PARITY: the partitioner returns a compaction descriptor (sectionGapPx, gridRowGapPx, cardPadPx, titleMarginPx); smartEngine.css reads the grid row gap, card padding and title margins from CSS variables with today's values as defaults; SmartResumeComposer applies the descriptor as inline variables on the page root, so the painted geometry is exactly the estimated geometry and the zero-footer-overlap invariant holds at every tier. UX STATES: the page-1 empty-space state is the defect under repair, and the loading/error surfaces of the preview are untouched. ACCESSIBILITY: compaction changes only spacing, so the reading order, aria semantics and the at-or-above 4.5:1 contrast of card titles and metas are unchanged, and no control gains or loses keyboard focus. SECURITY: no auth, token or sanitize path is touched and no Bearer token is logged. PERFORMANCE: at most three O(n) packing passes over the already-built sections, no extra re-renders, the sub-100ms render budget and the sub-4.0s build budget are preserved. QA: a new dir070 suite with static and functional proofs, plus a headless Playwright census of the Babu M profile on Cv1 Modern Split proving zero blank void and zero footer overlap. No native OS console windows and no winget/cmd/PowerShell; all servers stay on XAMPP.

2. smartPartitioner.js: drive multi-tier micro-compaction - try tier 0, and when the result is two pages with a minor trailing overflow retry tier 1 then tier 2, adopting the first tier that fits ONE page and only then, returning the adopted tier so the renderer matches

3. smartPartitioner.js: enforce the Page 1 void prevention invariant inside applyOrphanGuard by computing the donor page void after a proposed move and refusing the move whenever it would exceed 80px or 10 percent of the usable capacity

4. smartPartitioner.js: implement balanced 2-page distribution - keep greedy page-1 filling by splitting a section whenever at least one row fits, and when a section cannot start at all choose the smallest possible void so Page 1 fills to at least 85 percent of capacity whenever two pages are produced
5. smartPartitioner.js: return a compaction descriptor (sectionGapPx, gridRowGapPx, cardPadPx, titleMarginPx) while keeping sectionGapPx for backward compatibility

title: [Plan] DIR-071: DIR-071: Recruiter Applicant ATS Pipeline Word/PDF Export Fix & Global Candidate Photo Visibility Toggle Enforcement
body: DIR-071 P0, reconnaissance complete with every finding cited to file:line. CONTRACTS/INVARIANTS: XAMPP-only servers (no detached node/vite/nodemon), zero IDOR on the public export routes, the frozen 55 template modules stay untouched, and the DIR-063..070 suites plus the census and xampp-policy gates stay green. ROOT CAUSE OF THE RECRUITER EXPORT FAILURE: optionalAuth does not exist anywhere in the repository (a repo-wide grep matches only this directive spec). backend/index.js:465 short-circuits public paths with if (isPublicApiPath(req.path)) return next();, so req.user is NEVER populated on /api/public-export or /api/public-export-docx. The employer-claim branch I added in DIR-069 (index.js:4448 if (req.user?.uid) is therefore DEAD CODE that can never fire, and the PDF route (index.js:2441) has no claim branch at all - it goes straight to repo.getPublicResume and 404s an unpublished draft. That is the real defect, and the client-side withAuth:false at EmployerApplicantPipeline.jsx:317 is its mirror. (1) OPTIONAL AUTH MIDDLEWARE: in backend/security/auth.js I will extract the inline Bearer parsing (auth.js:115-117) into a shared helper and export optionalAuth(req,res,next) that decodes a present Bearer token into the SAME frozen req.user shape requireAuth builds, and calls next() when the header is absent or the token is invalid - it never 401s, so the public routes stay genuinely public. (2) WIRING: the /api public-path branch in backend/index.js will await optionalAuth before next(), so a recruiter Bearer token populates req.user on the public export routes. (3) EMPLOYER CLAIM ON BOTH ROUTES: I will extract the DIR-069 verification into ONE shared helper (require req.user.uid; repo.getJob(jobId).employerId === req.user.uid; the application must belong to that job AND reference exactly this resumeId) and call it from BOTH /api/public-export and /api/public-export-docx, so the two cannot drift. When verified the route exports the candidate's ACTUAL applied resume via repo.getResume(applicantId, resumeId) instead of 404ing or reading a stale public_resumes row; otherwise the strict published-only rule (isPublished true, publicationMode explicit) is unchanged. Zero IDOR: the employer id, the job id, the application id and the resume id must all agree server-side, and no client value is trusted as authority. (4) CLIENT: EmployerApplicantPipeline.jsx moves to withAuth:true and passes jobId from jobId ?? job_id and applicationId from applicationId ?? application_id ?? id, keeping the existing per-button loading state and the role=status error line. UX STATES: the drawer keeps its loading, busy and error surfaces; the fix removes a dead-end 404, and no new spinner or empty state is introduced. (5) GLOBAL PHOTO VISIBILITY SUPPRESSION: photo MUST be null whenever showPhoto is false (or hidePhoto true / includePhoto false). Confirmed gaps: (A) src/cv-templates/templateUtils.js:104 nulls only non-strings, never consulting showPhoto; (B) src/utils/resumeData.js:104-105 computes showPhoto but leaves photo intact; (C) MySQLRepository._resumeSnapshot:163-171 coerces showPhoto to a boolean but never nulls photo, so a hidden photo still ships in the public snapshot; (D) src/components/BuildResume/BuildResume.jsx:1142 exports the PDF after persistLatest({manual:true}) at 1133 without the visibility flag being authoritative. I will null the photo at every one of those four boundaries. SUPERSEDED CONTRACT FLAGGED HONESTLY: mandate 4A edits src/cv-templates/templateUtils.js while mandate 5 requires src/cv-templates to stay git diff 0 - those cannot both hold as written. templateUtils.js is the SHARED utility, not one of the 55 frozen template modules (cv1..cv51, cover1..cover4), so I will make the edit and re-scope the DIR-068 seal assertion to freeze the 55 template DIRECTORIES, reporting this supersession explicitly rather than silently weakening the seal. ACCESSIBILITY: no control is added or removed; the existing aria-labels, keyboard reachability and the at-or-above 4.5:1 contrast of the export buttons are unchanged. SECURITY: no token is ever logged, the Bearer value is never echoed to the client, error payloads keep the existing requestId contract with no plaintext secret leakage, and the new optionalAuth path cannot elevate a request because it only ever sets req.user and never grants a permission. PERFORMANCE: optionalAuth adds at most one verifyIdToken call on a request that already carries a Bearer token, public requests without one pay nothing, and the sub-4.0s build and sub-100ms render budgets are untouched. QA: a new tests/dir071-recruiter-export-photo-toggle.test.mjs with static contracts plus functional proofs that the claim rejects a foreign employer, a mismatched resumeId and a mismatched jobId, that the published-only fallback still 404s, and that photo is null under every visibility flag combination.

steps: 1. backend/security/auth.js: extract the inline Bearer regex from requireAuth into a shared tokenFromHeader helper and export a new optionalAuth middleware that decodes a present Bearer token into the same frozen req.user shape and always calls next(), never 401ing
2. backend/index.js: make the /api public-path branch await optionalAuth before next() so req.user is populated on public routes when a recruiter Bearer token is supplied

3. backend/index.js: extract the DIR-069 employer-claim verification into one shared helper that requires req.user.uid, checks repo.getJob(jobId).employerId === req.user.uid, and requires the application to belong to that job and reference exactly this resumeId

4. backend/index.js: call that helper from BOTH /api/public-export and /api/public-export-docx so the PDF route gains the claim it never had and the DOCX claim stops being dead code, exporting repo.getResume(applicantId, resumeId) when verified and keeping the strict published-only 404 fallback otherwise

5. src/components/EmployerPortal/EmployerApplicantPipeline.jsx: switch withAuth false to true and pass jobId from jobId ?? job_id and applicationId from applicationId ?? application_id ?? id, keeping the existing loading and role=status error surfaces

9. src/components/BuildResume/BuildResume.jsx: make the photo-visibility flag authoritative on the PDF and DOCX export path so a hidden photo is never exported

10. tests/dir071-recruiter-export-photo-toggle.test.mjs: static contracts (optionalAuth exported and wired, withAuth true, the shared claim helper used by both routes, the four photo boundaries) plus functional proofs (a foreign employer, a mismatched resumeId and a mismatched jobId are all rejected, the published-only fallback still 404s, and photo is null for every visibility flag combination)
11. re-scope the DIR-068 seal assertion to the 55 frozen template directories and report the templateUtils.js supersession explicitly

12. evidence: run npm run lint, test:security, test:product, test:templates, the DIR-063..071 suites, the census and xampp-policy gates and npm run build (verify sub-4.0s), confirm the 55 template dirs are unchanged, then submit via bridge dev submit-evidence.

ours is a flat list. 6 Job Portal (0 sticky) vs Wellfound/Indeed which lead with a sticky filter rail, saved searches and alerts - we have neither the rail nor alerts. 7 Job Tracker (Kanban from DIR-020, 9 grids, 18 breakpoints, 0 legacy) vs Huntr/Teal which add reminders and a pipeline HUD - ours has live sessions but no bounded split view and is the worst-styled surface in the suite. 10 Messages (lg split view from DIR-081) vs Linear/Slack which add a third details pane at xl plus a composer toolbar - ours has the content but no sticky rail and no Cuba styling. body: DIR-084 PHASES 1-3 forensics complete; this is the plan. ROOT CAUSE FOUND (PHASE 2 blocker): CubaAppShell.jsx:306 renders the shell root as w-full flex min-h-screen flex-col - min-h-screen, NOT a bounded height. The content row (CubaAppShell.jsx:522 w-full flex min-h-0 flex-1) and <main> (CubaAppShell.jsx:638 w-full min-w-0 flex-1 overflow-x-hidden) therefore never own the vertical scroll, so EVERY candidate page grows the DOCUMENT and the browser window scrollbar appears. That single line is why the whole suite violates the single-viewport paradigm. BLAST RADIUS: CubaAppShell is imported by CubaCandidateShell.jsx:7, CubaPortalShell.jsx:10 (employer/admin/enterprise) and DesignSystemShowcase.jsx:3, so a naive root change would alter four portals. The mandate is the Candidate Suite, so the plan adds an OPT-IN iewportLock prop that only CubaCandidateShell sets - the other portals keep today's behaviour byte for byte, which is both safer and exactly the requested scope. PHASE 1 OVERVIEW GEOMETRY (measured): the Overview stacks, in order, a breadcrumb row (mb-2.5, CubaAppShell.jsx:649), the content pad (pt-2.5 pb-24 md:pt-3 md:pb-6, :644), CubaCandidateHero (banner p-6 sm:p-8 at CubaCandidateHero.jsx:111, h1 	ext-2xl sm:text-3xl lg:text-4xl at :159, action row mt-6 at :168, ATS gauge panel p-4 at :194, and the FOUR stat cards at :253 in a gap-4 sm:gap-5 grid), AiCareerBriefing (about 90-120px), then the DashboardHomepage Document Gallery plus its four onboarding steps, all inside a space-y-4 md:space-y-5 wrapper (CubaCandidateShell.jsx:456) and a grid grid-cols-1 gap-6 xl:grid-cols-[minmax(0,7fr)_minmax(0,3fr)] (CubaCandidateShell.jsx:467) whose main column is space-y-6 and whose rail (CandidateExecutiveRail.jsx:99) is space-y-4. At 1080p that stack is roughly 900-1300px tall against a ~937px viewport, so the Hero, the 4 Stat Cards, the Briefing and the Rail can never be visible together - exactly the user complaint. The fix is to lock the region AND compact it: wrapper space-y-2.5, grid gap-3 promoted to 2xl, main column space-y-3, hero banner p-4 sm:p-5, h1 	ext-xl sm:text-2xl lg:text-3xl, action row mt-4, gauge p-3, stat grid gap-2.5 sm:gap-3, rail space-y-2.5 with internal scrolling, and the Document Gallery plus Onboarding moved into an internally-scrolling lower region so they never push the fold. PHASE 3 TOKENS AND SMOOTHNESS: the touched surfaces stay on Cuba tokens with dark: counterparts wherever a raw utility must remain, scroll owners gain scrollbar-gutter: stable so the appearance of a scrollbar cannot shift the layout, and the interactive controls keep their transitions. INVARIANTS: XAMPP-only servers, no detached node/vite/nodemon daemon; frozen src/cv-templates diff 0; no auth, token, API, DB or RBAC change; zero fabricated data - no metric, count or telemetry value is invented and the existing real bindings (count, bestScore, applications, trackedJobs, onboarding progress) are preserved; preserve every DIR-048/055/072-083 pin and the dir081/dir082/dir083 suites; sub-4s build; 0 lint errors. UX STATES: every page keeps the DIR-081 four-state contract and every split view keeps its below-lg single-pane fallback; the locked region must still render loading, empty and error states in full. RESPONSIVE: 375px keeps the single column with the mobile tab bar and its pb-24 reserve; 768px two columns; 1080p and 1440p are the single-viewport targets; 1680px+ keeps the wide cap. QA: tests/dir084-single-viewport-mastery.test.mjs with AC1 the viewportLock contract (root h-[100dvh] min-h-0 overflow-hidden, main min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto, aside h-full) and the opt-in default, AC2 the compacted Overview geometry, AC3 the Hero, the four stat cards, the Briefing and the Rail all inside ONE bounded region, AC4 no document-level min-h-screen remains on any of the 15 candidate page roots, AC5 dark-mode parity on every touched file, AC6 the interactive-control inventory is preserved, AC7 no new dependency and the build stays under 4s, AC8 no layout-shift hazard (scrollbar-gutter stable on the scroll owners). A11Y: the locked region keeps one main landmark and its skip target (cuba-main-content), the scroll owner stays keyboard reachable, focus is not trapped by the lock, aria-current and the labelled regions from DIR-083 are preserved, and contrast stays AA in both themes. PERFORMANCE: the change is layout-only - no new dependency, no timer, no simulated latency - and it should REDUCE paint cost because a bounded scroll region avoids whole-document reflow on every interaction. SEQUENCING AND RISK: the shell prop first (one file, opt-in), then the Overview compaction, then the per-page verification, then the token and smoothness pass. ROLLBACK: reverting the single opt-in prop restores today's document-scroll behaviour for the candidate suite, and each compaction is independently revertible; no schema, API or data surface is touched.

title: [Evidence] DIR-084: Candidate Suite Single-Viewport Golden 10/10 Master Layout Refactor & Zero-Gap Functional Verification
body: DIR-084 complete. ROOT CAUSE found in recon: CubaAppShell.jsx rendered the shell root as w-full flex min-h-screen flex-col - min-h-screen, NOT a bounded height - so the content row and main never owned the vertical scroll and EVERY candidate page grew the DOCUMENT, producing the browser window scrollbar. S1: because CubaAppShell is shared by the candidate shell, CubaPortalShell (employer/admin/enterprise) and DesignSystemShowcase, the fix is an OPT-IN viewportLock prop that only CubaCandidateShell sets. Under the lock the root becomes h-[100dvh] min-h-0 overflow-hidden, the content row becomes min-h-0 overflow-hidden, the sidebar rail becomes h-full, and main gains data-viewport-lock plus min-h-0 overflow-y-auto cuba-scrollbar [scrollbar-gutter:stable] so main owns the ONLY scrollbar and its appearance can never shift layout; the content cap compacted to min-h-0 px-4 pt-2 pb-24 sm:px-6 md:pt-2.5 md:pb-4 lg:px-8 and the breadcrumb to mb-2. The default is false, so the other portals keep today's behaviour byte for byte and the suite asserts they do not opt in. S2-S4 SINGLE-VIEWPORT OVERVIEW: the wrapper is space-y-2.5 on the Overview; the grid is grid min-h-0 grid-cols-1 gap-3 2xl:h-[calc(100dvh-var(--cuba-header-h)-3.75rem)] 2xl:grid-cols-[minmax(0,7fr)_minmax(0,3fr)] so on 1080p (1920px) and 1440p (2560px), both wider than the 1536px 2xl breakpoint, the entire Overview is bounded to exactly one viewport; the main column is a flex column whose fold-critical blocks are flex-none and whose children region is min-h-0 flex-1 2xl:overflow-y-auto with a stable gutter, and the rail is 2xl:overflow-y-auto with a stable gutter. Hero compacted: banner p-6 sm:p-8 to p-4 sm:p-5, h1 text-2xl sm:text-3xl lg:text-4xl to text-xl sm:text-2xl lg:text-3xl, action row mt-6 to mt-4, ATS gauge p-4 to p-3, and the four-card KPI grid gap-4 sm:gap-5 to gap-2.5 sm:gap-3. CandidateExecutiveRail space-y-4 to space-y-2.5 and AiCareerBriefing space-y-3 to space-y-2. Result: the Hero, the four Stat Cards, the AI Briefing and the Executive Rail are all visible together with zero document scrollbar. S5: DashboardHomepage's Overview branch compacted to space-y-3 and the Document Gallery plus the four onboarding steps moved into the internally-scrolling children region so they never push the fold. S6: six document-level min-h-screen page roots removed - DashboardPortfolios, DashboardInterviews, DashboardSettings and DashboardSupport now use min-h-0 with Cuba canvas/ink tokens, MainJobListings scopes min-h-screen to the public marketing route only, and DashboardHomepage keeps it only in the legacy non-Cuba branch. S8: new tests/dir084-single-viewport-mastery.test.mjs with 8 acceptance tests (AC1 the opt-in lock contract and the proof the other portals do not opt in, AC2 the compacted Overview geometry, AC3 Hero plus four Stat Cards plus Briefing plus Rail inside ONE bounded region, AC4 no document-level min-h-screen page root, AC5 Cuba tokens and no legacy palette on the touched roots, AC6 the interactive-control inventory preserved, AC7 the import allowlist plus a timer ratchet proving no dependency or timer was added, AC8 the stable scrollbar gutter on every scroll owner) and test:dir084 registered; four superseded pins updated in lockstep (DIR-048/077/078 content-cap and breadcrumb, the DIR-078 wrapper assertion and the unlayered-css-guard shell-root assertion). VERIFIED: dir084 8 passing, 149 passing across dir084 + dir083 + dir082 + dir081 + dir080 + dir079 + dir078 + dir077 + dir048 suites + dir055 + cuba-candidate-portal + cuba-design-system + copilot-command-surface, test:dir072..dir084 and test:design-system every script EXIT 0, test:product EXIT 0, security:static 67 passing, xampp-policy 4 passing, build EXIT 0 in 3.41s measured with no concurrent load against a 4.0s budget, lint 0 errors, frozen cv-templates diff 0. MEASUREMENT NOTE: two earlier build readings of 4.71s and 4.99s were taken while the full product and security suites were running in parallel on the same machine; isolated the build is 3.41s. HONEST LIMITS: the lock is opt-in so the employer/admin/enterprise portals were not migrated and that is not claimed; the Overview single-viewport guarantee is scoped to the 2xl breakpoint which covers both mandated targets, while 1280-1535px keeps natural flow; and the wider DIR-082 legacy backlog is unchanged and still ratcheted (DashboardSettings 1330, DashboardInterviews 764, DashboardHomepage 226, DashboardSupport 183, ResumesList 12) - DIR-084 fixed those pages' ROOT palettes but did not sweep their bodies. The four stat cards alone are ~120px each plus gap, so hero + cards + briefing consume roughly 500px of a ~937px 1080p viewport before a single resume is drawn - which is exactly the user's complaint that the resume workspace is a cut-off bottom sliver. (2) TRIPLE DUPLICATION is real and measurable: the hero cards show Active Resumes, Average ATS Score, Job Applications and AI Interview Coach; the right rail (CandidateExecutiveRail.jsx) independently renders an ATS Keyword Strength widget at :129 and an Application Milestones widget at :153; and DashboardHomepage additionally renders a legacy Career Command Center block at :1040-1175 that recomputes calculateAtsScore at :1046 and prints an ATS score at :1101 (it early-returns null for the Cuba shell at :1042, so it is dead weight in the Cuba chrome but the duplication pattern is the same). ATS therefore appears as a headline in TWO places and applications in TWO places. (3) THE COLD RADAR is AtsRadialGauge, imported from StatMicroVisuals.jsx:15 and rendered at CubaCandidateHero.jsx:273 - a bare 56px circle with no character, which is what reads as sterile rather than as a native AI engine. (4) THE WORKSPACE ALREADY EXISTS but is buried: DashboardHomepage already has category pills at :1180-1185, a search box at :1192-1199, per-card ATS badges computed from the REAL calculateAtsScore(document.item)?.qualityScore at :1399, and the card list at :1371+. So the mandate is NOT to invent a workspace but to PROMOTE the existing one above the fold and de-duplicate the metrics. (5) NO MASCOT ASSET EXISTS anywhere under src/assets (I searched every png/svg/webp/gif for mascot/robot/pilot/ai/bot/avatar/illustration and found only trustpilot.png and payment/country icons), so the mascot must be an inline SVG component - no new binary and no new dependency. The design system already ships the right tokens for it: cuba-tokens.css defines --cuba-ai-aurora-a and --cuba-ai-aurora-b, so the glowing aurora halo can be token-driven rather than a hardcoded gradient. PHASE 1 COMPACT AI COPILOT HERO (~90-110px): a new CubaCopilotMascot.jsx renders a friendly inline-SVG AI robot/avatar (rounded head, glowing eyes, antenna, warm smile) inside an aurora halo built from the existing aurora tokens, and a new CopilotHeroHud.jsx renders a single horizontal glass row at py-3: mascot + a PilotAI Copilot Active status pill with a real live indicator + a dynamic career insight line taken from the EXISTING briefingLogic output (never invented) + three compact CTAs (New Resume, Explore Jobs, Mock Drill) wired to the real routes already used elsewhere in the app. It REPLACES the tall gradient banner, so the ~500px hero becomes ~100px. PHASE 2 COMPACT METRIC CAPSULE STRIP (~45-55px): a new CubaMetricCapsule.jsx renders one tight horizontal glass row of four capsules - Resumes, ATS, Applications, Interview Coach Ready - bound to the SAME real values the hero cards used today (count, bestScore from the real ATS calculation, applications, readiness). The four CubaStatCards and the AtsRadialGauge are removed from the hero, so the strip is the ONLY place a headline metric is printed. DE-DUPLICATION RULE, enforced by test: a metric may appear ONCE as a headline (the capsule strip) and at most ONCE as a detail view (the rail), never twice as a headline. The rail keeps its ATS Keyword Strength and Application Milestones widgets as DETAIL views with their existing breakdowns. PHASE 3 ABOVE-THE-FOLD RESUME WORKSPACE: the main left column (~68%, already the 7fr of the existing 7fr/3fr split) leads with the resume workspace instead of the hero: the EXISTING category pills, search and sort, and high-density resume cards with a thumbnail, an ATS badge from the real per-card score, and one-click Edit, Tailor AI and PDF Download actions, all immediately browsable inside the single viewport. The right column (~32%, the existing 3fr) keeps the AI Career Briefing and the Live Copilot Quick-Pitch. The onboarding steps move BELOW the workspace inside the already-internally-scrolling children region so they never push the fold. INVARIANTS: XAMPP-only servers, no detached node/vite/nodemon daemon; frozen src/cv-templates diff 0 (the resume thumbnails and the PDF download path are READ-ONLY consumers); no auth, token, API, DB or RBAC change; ZERO FABRICATED DATA - every number in the hero, the capsules and the cards binds to an existing real source (the same count/bestScore/applications/readiness the hero uses today and the same calculateAtsScore result the cards already compute), and an absent value renders an honest empty state rather than a placeholder figure; preserve every DIR-048/055/072-084 pin and the dir081-dir084 suites; sub-4s build; 0 lint errors. UX STATES: the workspace keeps the DIR-081 four-state contract (ready/loading/empty/error) with a CubaSkeleton card grid while loading and the existing CubaEmptyState when there are no documents; the new HUD and capsules must render honest states rather than zeros when the underlying read has not resolved. RESPONSIVE: 375px stacks HUD, capsules, then the workspace as a single column with the cards at full width; 768px two capsules per row and a two-column card grid; 1080p and 1440p are the single-viewport targets where the whole command centre including the resume cards is above the fold; the DIR-084 viewport lock and its stable scrollbar gutter are preserved. QA: tests/dir085-overview-workspace-mastery.test.mjs with AC1 the compact HUD and capsule strip exist and the four old stat cards plus the radial gauge are gone from the hero; AC2 the workspace is the FIRST block in the main column and the onboarding follows it; AC3 the de-duplication rule holds (no headline metric is printed twice); AC4 zero whole-window scroll (the DIR-084 lock is intact and the Overview grid stays viewport-bounded); AC5 a11y - the mascot is decorative with aria-hidden, the status pill and capsules are labelled, the CTAs keep their accessible names, and contrast stays AA in both themes; AC6 no new dependency, no new binary asset, build under 4s and no fabricated telemetry. A11Y: the mascot is aria-hidden decoration with a text equivalent in the status pill, the capsule strip is a labelled list, the workspace pills keep aria-pressed, the card actions keep their labels, focus-visible is preserved and nothing relies on colour alone. PERFORMANCE: the mascot is inline SVG (no network request, no new dependency), the capsules replace four heavier cards, and the compaction REDUCES paint cost because fewer nodes render above the fold; the build stays under 4s. SEQUENCING AND RISK: mascot and capsules first (new, isolated components), then the hero swap, then the workspace promotion, then the tests. ROLLBACK: each new component is additive and the hero swap is a single edit, so reverting restores today's layout exactly; no schema, API or data surface is touched.

title: [Plan] DIR-086: Candidate Overview 10/10 Polish — Zero Horizontal Scrollbars, Working Copilot Quick-Pitch Routing, Compact Action Cards & Streamlined Rail
body: DIR-086 recon complete. FOUR defects confirmed with file:line evidence. (1) THE QUICK-PITCH NO-OP: CandidateExecutiveRail.jsx:106 computes href as action.routes[0], and in copilotActions.js all three candidate actions list /dashboard FIRST - candidate-tailor-resume routes ['/dashboard','/build-resume'] at :55, candidate-cover-letter routes ['/dashboard','/cover-letter'] at :65, candidate-mock-interview routes ['/dashboard','/dashboard/interview'] at :75 - so every Quick-Pitch click resolves to /dashboard, the page the user is already on. candidate-mock-interview even carries the correct navigateTo '/dashboard/interview' at :84 but the rail never reads it, and '/cover-letter' at :65 is not a mounted route at all (the real one is '/dashboard/cover-letters'). (2) THE AWKWARD SCROLLBAR TRACK: the category pill row at DashboardHomepage.jsx:1179 is 'flex items-center gap-1.5 overflow-x-auto pb-1 md:pb-0' with no scrollbar styling, so the browser paints its native track. WORSE, the class the repo already uses for this - scrollbar-none at EducationStep.jsx:469 and WorkHistoryStep.jsx:2285 - is a NO-OP: package.json pins tailwindcss ^4.1.8 and NO scrollbar plugin is installed, so it generates no CSS. The real fix is the Tailwind v4 arbitrary form [scrollbar-width:none] plus [&::-webkit-scrollbar]:hidden, which needs no plugin. (3) CARD CLUTTER: the resume card renders a primary button at :1552 and then a grid grid-cols-2 of FOUR full-width secondary buttons spanning :1566-1650 (Edit, PDF, Word, Share) while an overflow menu ALREADY exists at :1460-1490 - that is the stacked-button wall in the screenshot. (4) RAIL DUPLICATION: CandidateExecutiveRail renders three WidgetCards - Live Copilot Quick-Pitch at :100, ATS Keyword Strength at :129 and Application Milestones at :153 - and the last two repeat exactly what the DIR-085 capsule strip already shows, which is why the rail overflows. PLAN. S1 routing: give each candidate action an explicit navigateTo (tailor -> /build-resume/heading, cover letter -> /dashboard/cover-letters, mock interview -> /dashboard/interview), reorder their routes so /dashboard is never first, and make the rail PREFER navigateTo and otherwise fall back to the MOST SPECIFIC route rather than routes[0], so no action can resolve to a no-op again. S2 scrollbars: hide the native track with the Tailwind v4 arbitrary utilities and repair the two no-op scrollbar-none usages, keeping every row scrollable and keyboard reachable. S3 card: one primary Edit Resume plus icon-only PDF and Word actions plus the EXISTING overflow menu, each with an accessible name and a 44px target. S4 rail: delete the ATS Keyword Strength and Application Milestones widgets so the rail holds only the Live Copilot Quick-Pitch and fits the viewport. INVARIANTS: XAMPP-only servers, no detached node/vite/nodemon daemon; frozen src/cv-templates diff 0; no auth, token, API, DB or RBAC change since every fix is presentational or a navigation target; ZERO FABRICATED DATA - the rail stops repeating real figures rather than inventing replacements; preserve every DIR-048/055/072-085 pin and the dir081-dir085 suites; sub-4s build; 0 lint errors. UX STATES: removing two rail widgets must not remove their empty-state handling - the Quick-Pitch keeps its CubaEmptyState - and the card keeps its download and share gating (allowsPdfExport / allowsDocxDownload / allowsShareLink) so a non-premium user still sees the honest locked state rather than a broken button. RESPONSIVE: the icon actions stay tappable at 375px, the pill row scrolls without a visible track at every width, and the streamlined card reduces height so more cards sit above the fold at 1080p. QA: tests/dir086-candidate-overview-polish.test.mjs with AC1 the three candidate actions resolve to their real destinations and none resolves to /dashboard, AC2 the rail prefers navigateTo and no longer renders the ATS or milestone widgets, AC3 the pill row hides its scrollbar with a real utility and the repo no longer relies on the no-op scrollbar-none, AC4 the card exposes one primary Edit plus PDF and Word icon actions plus the overflow menu, AC5 a11y with accessible names and the overflow menu roles, AC6 no new dependency and the build stays under 4s. A11Y: the icon-only PDF and Word buttons carry aria-labels, the overflow menu keeps role=menu/menuitem and its Escape dismissal, the pill row stays keyboard scrollable with focus-visible, and contrast stays AA in both themes. PERFORMANCE: no new dependency and no timer, and removing two rail widgets plus three card buttons REDUCES node count and paint work so build and first paint improve. SEQUENCING AND RISK: the routing fix first (the user-visible bug), then the scrollbar utility, then the card and rail simplification, then the tests. ROLLBACK: each fix is independently revertible; no schema, API or data surface is touched.

I am stating that first because the rest of this summary should not be read as claiming the headline number. S1 MEASUREMENT HARNESS BUILT FIRST: .bridge/evidence/dir088-builder-score.mjs scores the whole BuildResume module with the same derived formula DIR-087 used (score = 10 * (0.50*tokenAdoption + 0.25*responsive + 0.25*guards)) and is imported by the test suite, so the number is enforced rather than asserted. MEASURED BASELINE was score 1.2 with 2252 legacy colour utilities and 8 cuba classes across 37 files. NOTE ON THE BRIEF: its figure of 235 is only BuildResume.jsx itself; the module-wide total is 2252, and every one of the 32 component files had ZERO cuba- classes except BuildResume.jsx with 8, so this was a from-scratch tokenisation rather than a touch-up. S2 MAPPING TABLE WITH SEMANTIC SAFETY: I measured the families before transforming anything and found 1073 neutral (slate/gray/zinc/neutral/stone) plus 1179 semantic (red/green/amber/blue/...), summing exactly to the 2252 the DIR-087 counter reported. I did NOT run a blind find-and-replace, for a reason I verified in the tokens themselves: --cuba-pill-success-fill is #1a7f37, a SOLID green, and --cuba-pill-success-ink is #ffffff, WHITE. The Cuba pill tokens are SOLID BADGES, not tints, so remapping a light tint such as bg-green-50 onto a pill token would turn a subtle wash into a solid block. Light tints need the -soft rgba variants instead. The transformer therefore carries an explicit auditable table and refuses to guess at the semantic families. S3 WHAT WAS TOKENISED: .bridge/evidence/dir088-tokenize.mjs substituted only the neutral structural families, where every shade has a documented 1:1 equivalent (slate-50 to --cuba-canvas, slate-200 to --cuba-line, slate-900 to --cuba-ink). RESULT 1072 substitutions across 32 files; measured after: legacy 2252 to 1180, cuba 8 to 1095, tokenAdoption 0.004 to 0.481, score 1.2 to 3.5. One case is deliberately left alone and asserted as such: shadow-slate-200 sets a shadow COLOUR while the Cuba shadow tokens are SIZES, so a mechanical swap would have changed the utility type. S4 REZI-GRADE INLINE ATS, BUILT ON THE REAL ENGINE: the project already owns a 1168-line ATS engine at src/utils/atsScore.js, so the inline guidance is built ON it rather than inventing a second scorer - action-verb power hints from leadingActionVerb plus ACTION_VERBS, bullet length benchmarks from extractBullets, keyword density cues from extractJdKeywords plus keywordOccursInText, and section verdicts from calculateAtsScore().sections[].findings. Wired into StepShell.jsx in BOTH the desktop sticky rail and the mobile accordion, so all 13 steps inherit it from one wrapper instead of each editor reimplementing it, and when the engine has nothing to say the panel renders an explicit Nothing to flag yet line rather than a fabricated tip. My tokenisation changed it, the product suite caught it, and I updated the pin to the tokenised class while keeping the full class list locked, so the scope class, geometry and overflow behaviour all remain pinned. I did not weaken the assertion to make it pass. TWO TRAPS THE TABLE EXISTS TO AVOID, both verified in src/styles/cuba-tokens.css: first, --cuba-primary-ink is #ffffff WHITE, so mapping text-indigo-600 onto it would make dark accent text invisible on light surfaces, and accent text therefore maps to --cuba-primary-ink-strong (#4b3ec4) while light indigo text on dark fills maps to --cuba-ink-inverse; second, the --cuba-pill-*-fill tokens are SOLID badges with WHITE ink (the DIR-088 lesson), so light tints map to the -soft rgba variants and never onto a pill token.
